rationale: Arithmetically this is little more than the already-tested NetWorkingCapitalClaimsProfit (claims net of payables, α 4.2%, t 4.58) with the cash balance moved into the numerator and the scaling switched from assets to claims, so it is a repackaging of two validated legs rather than a new characteristic, and che/(act−che) is a monotone transform of the archive's che/act leg.

The pairing of the claim-deflated profitability leg with the cash-share leg genuinely has not been run, and both parents are strong, but note the two legs are mechanically positively correlated (both reward a small act−che), so the MIN may collapse toward a single low-working-capital characteristic — worth testing precisely to see whether the conjunction adds anything beyond that.

Deflating claims by sales and payables by cost is the economically correct construction of a cash conversion cycle and is a real ordering difference from the netted-stock leg already tested; the main risks are instability when sale or cogs are small and correlation with the known operating-cycle/net-working-capital results, not conceptual redundancy.

This is a template clone of ProfitPlusConditionalLiquidityBonus with only the bonus leg swapped, and since the additive z-score of gross profitability dominates that structure the result is near-guaranteed to reproduce the earlier alpha without isolating the supplier-funding mechanism; the claimed sign flip for loss firms is asserted rather than motivated.

This is ProfitableButClaimBloated (already tested, α −2.2%, t −2.21) with gross claims replaced by claims net of payables — a single-term substitution on an existing short-side test, and the expected gain is unlikely given the mirror-image long form has already been measured.

Because the claim stock is benchmarked against its own five-year minimum with no sales or asset scaling, the leg mechanically measures five-year growth in working capital and will largely proxy the asset-growth anomaly rather than the "slack above operating necessity" the hypothesis describes; scaling both current and minimum claims by sales would make the expression match the stated economics.
